Today the toolkit can score a return series but it can't hand back a structured period-by-period walk-forward view that lists each window and then summarizes them together. Add a new, separate report for this.

Expose a function importable from the package top level as `walk_forward_report(returns, train_size, test_size)` that returns a dict with two keys: `rows` (one entry per evaluation window, each entry carrying `test_start`, `test_end`, `mean_return`, `win_rate`, and `max_drawdown`) and `summary` (with `num_windows`, `mean_return` = mean of the window returns, `win_rate` = mean of the window win rates, and `max_drawdown` = the worst window drawdown). This is a distinct new entry point from any existing single-number evaluation. A series too short for any window must return an empty `rows` list and a zeroed `summary`, not raise.
issue_title: Analysts can't get a period-by-period walk-forward evaluation report
issue_body:
When an analyst evaluates a strategy over time, they want to see how it held up across successive periods rather than a single blended number. Today the toolkit can score a return series but it can't hand back a structured period-by-period walk-forward view that lists each window and then summarizes them together. Add a new, separate report for this.

Expose a function importable from the package top level as `walk_forward_report(returns, train_size, test_size)` that returns a dict with two keys: `rows` (one entry per evaluation window, each entry carrying `test_start`, `test_end`, `mean_return`, `win_rate`, and `max_drawdown`) and `summary` (with `num_windows`, `mean_return` = mean of the window returns, `win_rate` = mean of the window win rates, and `max_drawdown` = the worst window drawdown). This is a distinct new entry point from any existing single-number evaluation. A series too short for any window must return an empty `rows` list and a zeroed `summary`, not raise.
expected_behavior: `walk_forward_report(returns, train_size, test_size)` is importable from the package top level and returns a dict with `rows` and `summary`.
`rows` has one entry per evaluation window, each with `test_start`, `test_end`, `mean_return`, `win_rate`, and `max_drawdown`.
`summary` reports `num_windows`, the mean window `mean_return`, the mean window `win_rate`, and the worst window `max_drawdown`.
A series too short for any window yields an empty `rows` list and a zeroed `summary` rather than an error.
Existing evaluation and backtest behavior is unchanged.
expected_failure_summary: The package has no walk-forward report: there is no function that returns per-window rows plus an aggregate summary over the windows.
task_author_notes: Stage 1 of the marketlab_walkforward group. Reference adds marketlab/walkforward_report.py with walk_forward_report (per-window rows + summary) reusing the existing walk_forward_eval, exported via __init__.py. A clean, general single-series report builder (build_window_rows + summarize_rows that operate on one series) makes Stage 2 (per-symbol grouping) a thin loop; a hardcoded single-series path forces a rewrite, measured as extension friction.
